newsitem.title: ITALY: Gucci --CSFB sees Q3 sales up 62 percent.
newsitem.headline: Gucci --CSFB sees Q3 sales up 62 percent.

text.p: Italian luxury goods group Gucci is expected to report a 62 percent surge in 1996 third quarter sales (August-October), forecasts CS First Boston in a note with the investment bank maintaining its "buy" stance on the stock.
The bank expects Gucci third quarter revenue of $220 million (including royalities) after $136 million in the Q3 1995, when the group reports its results on November 21.

CSFB analyst Cedric Magnelia said that leather goods probably recorded the strongest growth in the third quarter followed closely by shoes, while retail sales remain strong in part supplemented by recently opened own stores
He suspects Gucci's growth is truly explosive in south east Asia and very strong in Japan particularly as the company is underdistributed in these markets in comparison with its competitors.
He sees cumulative nine months sales (Feb-Oct) up 78 percent to $610 million after $342 million.

For full year results to end-January 1997, CSFB forecast $862 million in revenues, operating profits of $220 million (margin of 26.7 percent against 25.5 percent in 1995) and net earnings of $146 million against $81 million.
